maxent_evaluator.tie_convention: The probabilistic evaluator assigns mass to every enumerated candidate; the source's categorical-success criterion compares summed overt probabilities rather than declaring a tie-breaking winner.

hidden_structure_consumer.success_criterion: the summed probability of every full structure with the correct SR is greater than the corresponding sum for any other SR

candidate_support.ur_generation: A UR is included for an input only when a corresponding input-to-UR constraint exists; the source adds such constraints from observed SRs.
candidate_support.stress_length_fragment: Candidate SRs are stated to include every combination of root-only or suffix-only stress and faithful or shortened long vowels for each admitted UR.
candidate_support.display_omissions: Table 7 rounds probabilities to two decimals and omits candidates whose displayed probability rounds to zero.
candidate_support.complete_score_ledger: The source does not print every omitted candidate's exact Harmony or probability.

scaling_statement.transformation: multiply every constraint weight by one common positive constant
scaling_statement.printed_claim: For a MaxEnt grammar meeting the source's summed-probability success criterion, the probabilities of the correct forms can be made arbitrarily close to one by scaling the weights.

project_derived_uses: The application classifies the scaling claim as a generated corollary of the closed fixed-support response theorem, not as an additional registered theorem.
For fixed finite support, the target overt probability converges to one exactly when every globally best hidden candidate belongs to the target overt fibre.

An exact four-parse counterwitness has three target-fibre parses one score unit below one wrong-fibre parse. At positive scale log(2), the target aggregate is 3/5 and therefore satisfies the source's strict overt-fibre success criterion; further common scaling crosses 1/2 at log(3) and converges to zero, not one.
The application does not reclassify Table 7 because the rounded display is not a complete exact score ledger.
scope_ceiling: This transcription licenses the source's hidden-candidate MaxEnt formula, overt-fibre consumer, displayed success criterion, and common-scaling statement. It does not prove the omitted score ledger, the learner's convergence, infinite-support asymptotics, or a hidden representation from overt data alone.

anchors.transcribed_role: MaxEnt Harmony, partition function, hidden (UR,SR) candidates, and overt-fibre summation
candidate construction, rounded-zero omissions, and summed correct-SR success criterion

source_claims: Observed SR probability is the sum of the probabilities of all admitted hidden (UR,SR) candidates with that SR.
The categorical simulation is called successful when correct-SR aggregate probability exceeds every rival-SR aggregate probability.
The source states that common positive weight scaling can make correct-form probability arbitrarily close to one.
